newsitem.title: UK: National Express chief executive resigns.
newsitem.headline: National Express chief executive resigns.

text.p: British passenger transport group National Express Group Plc said on Tuesday its group chief executive Ernest Patterson had resigned with immediate effect.

In a statement the company gave no reason for the move, but said that it had been after mutual agreement. Patterson will be replaced by Phil White, currently director in charge of its West Midlands Travel unit.
The statement also quoted group chairman Michael Davies as saying that the company remained confident about current trading.

"Although the 1996 financial results are not yet available, I can confirm that based on our latest estimates the group has traded well across all its divisions in the second half of 1996 and looks forward to 1997 with confidence," he said.

In a reaffirmation of group strategy, he added that National Express was still committed to increasing value for shareholders "through the expansion and development of existing businesses and through acquisitions in existing and related areas".
The surprise news triggered a mark-down in the group's share price and before the full opening of the market National Express shares were indicated 17-1/2p lower at 526-1/2p.
